Backend and transcript regressions validate native meaning and reject invalid scores; see tests/test_asr_decoder_evidence.py and tests/test_asr_optional_runtime_dependencies.py. Multiple hypotheses and calibrated uncertainty remain unavailable. - **MTA-ASR-I15:** Research summary and paper section are present in `docs/asr-rnd-research-section.md`, covering the hypothesis, method, baselines, negative findings, novelty limits, ablation gaps, ethics and reproducibility pointers. No novel clinical acoustic reranking claim is made; related-work comparison and the full matched-compute ablation matrix remain open.

tasks.requirement: Create a lossless span-coverage ledger from original audio to every proposed model window. **
tasks.acceptance: ** No source speech span is omitted, silently truncated or duplicated in the output mapping.

progress_evidence.text: - **MTA-ASR-C03:** The planner emits a coverage ledger that detects omitted and duplicated annotated source spans; VAD and pause-aware candidates fail closed if the supplied speech spans are not covered. Tests cover gaps and overlap duplication. Status: partial; no annotated speech-span WAV set is available for measuring real source coverage, and the current ledger is a pure planner primitive rather than a runtime publication gate. - **MTA-ASR-C04:** Added stitching that requires one output per stable segment ID, orders by source offsets, and deduplicates exact suffix/prefix tokens only when the windows overlap. Every removal is marked for audio review; non-overlapping repeated words are preserved. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py covers repeated edges, true non-overlap repetitions, and missing outputs. Status: partial; no measured word timestamps exist to disambiguate a true repeated word that happens at an overlapping window edge. - **MTA-ASR-C05:** Added tunable VAD candidate minimum duration, maximum duration, and padding, preserving source sample offsets and checking supplied speech-span coverage. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py exercises short-span padding, duration limits, and coverage failures. Status: partial; thresholds have not been ablated against matched frozen conversations. - **MTA-ASR-C06:** Added source-span diagnostics for omitted short turns, window-edge clips, partial coverage, joined known roles, and windows carrying unknown-role turns. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py verifies each category. Status: partial; no annotated conversation audio is available to generate measured boundary reports. - **MTA-ASR-C09:** Added inverse source-frame/window-frame mapping keyed by stable window ID, returning channel identity where applicable. Round-trip tests cover fixed crops and channel-first windows. Status: partial; the helper covers same-rate sample-index crops; resampled audio must use the separate measured-delay mapping contract, and runtime transcript integration remains pending. - **MTA-ASR-C08:** Added regression cases for exact shared suffix/prefix, backtracking around a shared medical phrase, and repeated metformin mentions in an overlap. tests/test_overlap_stitch_integrity.py exercises the existing sequence-alignment reassembler. Status: partial; alignment remains hypothesis-text-only and ambiguous repeated edge speech still requires original-audio review. - **MTA-ASR-C07:** Added bounded context handoff requiring an explicitly acoustically reviewed prior span and a current candidate-speech signal; silent or indeterminate current windows receive empty context. Tests verify bounded carryover and silence suppression. Status: partial; this contract is not yet wired into a long-form decoder, and candidate activity is a VAD heuristic rather than proof of speech. - **MTA-ASR-D02:** Added a typed ASR backend contract for inference, availability, timestamp capability, n-best capability, confidence capability, and runtime receipts. The faster-whisper adapter declares segment timestamps and explicitly unsupported n-best/confidence. Fake provider tests cover missing models, timeout exceptions, malformed output, and capability honesty. Status: partial; timeout propagation is tested as a provider failure, but no hard cancellation of a non-cooperative backend is implemented. - **MTA-ASR-D03:** Added an Omi backend candidate wrapper that requires the exact local GGUF digest, pinned runtime and existing CPU library; automatic downloads are disabled. It reports text-only output with no native timestamps, n-best, or confidence. Added tests/test_omi_backend.py for rejecting missing weights before runtime initialization. Status: partial; the focused pytest process stalled before collection and did not complete, and no production worker profile or inference-mode promotion is configured. - **MTA-ASR-D06:** Added normalized pairwise transcript disagreement with differing token spans. The output states that scores are uncalibrated, agreement is not truth, and no candidate selection occurs. tests/test_hypothesis_disagreement.py covers negation, dose substitution, agreement, and invalid candidate sets. Status: partial; thresholds have not been tuned against labeled disagreement cases and the diagnostic is not wired into runtime routing. Ruff and a direct substitution smoke check pass; focused pytest stalled before collection in this environment. - **MTA-ASR-D10:** Added a fail-closed candidate admission gate that requires failure-inclusive WER at or below the unchanged 5% maximum, validated source timing, reviewed licensing, passed critical-safety review, and matched evaluation. Tests cover exact gate boundary and each denial reason. Status: partial; no deployment promotion command is wired to this policy, so current profiles remain explicitly not admitted. - **MTA-ASR-D07:** Implemented and ran a post-hoc ROVER-style confusion-network vote on three frozen fixed-window engines over the same 16 consultation cases. Report evaluation/reports/rover-meddistract-detailed-v2-final.json SHA-256 4a47684f4b148bc57e8ce0bdde18665a108dfbc51e8cf39a3fae0063174b3f93 binds all source report hashes, model configuration digests, the frozen suite, and the ROVER/scorer code hashes. ROVER: 5,617/27,366 edits (20.525%); faster-whisper large-v3: 5,798 (21.187%); Parakeet: 6,071 (22.184%); Omi: 7,708 (28.166%). Two Omi failures are retained and mark those ROVER cases failed. tests/test_rover.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this unweighted voting baseline remains far above the 5% gate and has no clinical critical-token validation or inference-mode promotion. - **MTA-ASR-D08:** Added a sequential backend pool that closes the active model before loading another, serializes requests, and fails closed on lock timeout or MemoryError. Its receipt explicitly says memory admission was not measured. Tests cover switching, contention, and resource failure. Status: partial; the pool is not wired into the application worker and no full-process memory or 16 GB hardware admission test has been run. - **MTA-ASR-D09:** Generated a matched single/two-engine Pareto report from the frozen 16-case detailed runs. evaluation/reports/asr-compute-pareto-v1.json SHA-256 E909202756CF5D0F5383A9D81A14F3F86FA86F99878913C73EB82C7AA257B62C binds report, suite, model configuration, and code hashes. Single-engine p95 case wall RTFs: faster-whisper large-v3 2.082, Omi 0.294, Parakeet 0.106. Sequential faster-whisper plus Parakeet p95 RTF: 2.186. Two-engine WER equals the faster-whisper pivot because two-way token ties favor pivot; all arms fail the 5% gate. Peak ASR memory and CPU seconds are explicitly unknown; targeted fallback was not evaluated. tests/test_asr_pareto.py: 2 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; fresh resource measurements and a targeted-fallback arm remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-D04:** Added a Parakeet ONNX backend implementing the common backend contract. It verifies the exact local artifact set and digests, requires onnx-asr 0.12.0, uses CPU execution, disables downloads, and declares text-only output without timestamps or confidence. Tests cover missing weights and truthful capability receipts. Status: partial; although frozen Parakeet benchmark outputs exist, this new adapter is not integrated into application selected-window routing. - **MTA-ASR-E01:** Added a reproducible, provenance-bound English lexicon candidate artifact at evaluation/lexicons/clinical-english-v1-e01.json (SHA-256 af4b321287acd7762f6a9f63fe1ca29c4fc71ce0c52eda0ef95288efbfa4d142). The builder accepts only rights-reviewed, locked development manifests, rejects reserved acceptance groups, excludes uncertain reference rows, and records record/group IDs, reference hashes, offsets and dataset/manifest digests for each occurrence. It found one seed term (paracetamol) in eight licensed development references. tests/test_clinical_lexicon.py: 2 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the seed inventory is only the existing five generic opt-in hints, this artifact does not validate clinical terminology, and no backend consumes it for decoding or reranking. - **MTA-ASR-E02:** Added strict, immutable ASR clinical-entity schema kinds for drug name, strength, route, frequency, allergy, negation, anatomy, measurement and temporal relation. The current deterministic extractor emits only source-spanned medication and strength candidates, binds each strength to a medication, and keeps simple negated/uncertain clause status explicit. Tests disambiguate aspirin 75 mg from amlodipine 5 mg and a denied drug from an affirmed one; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this heuristic covers only simple English clauses, is not clinically validated, and does not yet emit the other declared entity types or route/frequency relations. - **MTA-ASR-E03:** Hardened the non-destructive ASR suggestion path. It now preserves a deep copy of raw segments, retains original text beside each proposal, marks every proposal review-required and non-adopted, and emits explicit reasons when medication identities or numeric/unit signatures differ. Invalid suggestion indexes fail closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this safeguards the helper contract, but the postprocessor is not yet the sole publication path for every runtime transcript workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E04:** Wired the pinned faster-whisper `hotwords` decoder hook to an optional, hash-pinned lexicon selection. Only terms present in the E01 provenance artifact are accepted; the adapter records candidate-only bias metadata and does not mutate text. The official faster-whisper interface documents `hotwords` as a decode hint. Focused adapter/context tests: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this permits only the single term currently present in the lexicon, and no paired bias/no-bias WER or false-insertion evaluation has been run, so it is not an admitted profile. - **MTA-ASR-E05:** Partial, resource-limited. The existing synthetic ASR challenge lists a generic `medical_homophone` case but contains no reviewed drug-name confusable pairs or clinical gold. The licensed development lexicon currently has one observed term, so it cannot support a meaningful sound-alike/abbreviation subgroup evaluation. Existing medication-binding checks cover explicit medication and dose swaps, but are not phonetic confusability evidence. No clinical correctness claim is made; completion requires an approved, rights-reviewed confusable set and reference labels. - **MTA-ASR-E09:** Partial, metadata-limited. Audited the six frozen development dataset manifests; none declares accent/dialect labels. No accent subgroups or accent identity were inferred from audio or names. Accordingly no accent-related accuracy result is reported. Completion requires legally available English mock data with actual reviewed metadata and a sufficient matched denominator. - **MTA-ASR-E06:** Added a finite candidate formatter limited to whitespace and case normalization for recognized numbers with supported explicit units. It verifies the before/after quantity signature, preserves the original string, never adds a missing unit, and never automatically adopts a candidate. Tests cover decimal/unit distinctions and unsupported or absent units; tests/test_asr_number_format.py: 3 passed and postprocess controls: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no additional unit systems or app publication integration are claimed. - **MTA-ASR-E08:** Ran a paired local faster-whisper tiny.en development pilot on four clean paracetamol-positive turns and four nearest non-target turns. evaluation/reports/asr-lexicon-bias-pilot-v1-final.json SHA-256 d2fa02f5c7a894a8cdd57c7a6bd99136241aa1350c6b86cdd60e0150f0b616a7 binds the frozen dataset/lock, profile, lexicon and evaluator/adapter code hashes. Exact-term recall changed 1/4 to 4/4, while false insertions changed 0/4 to 1/4 and normalized WER worsened from 44/153 (28.76%) to 46/153 (30.07%); no inference failures occurred. The result is development-only, not adjudicated clinical gold. Status: partial; this small pilot shows a non-target insertion and worse overall WER, and cannot justify enabling biasing or satisfy full-cohort validation. - **MTA-ASR-E07:** Added an ASR candidate comparison wrapper around the conservative source-vs-claim rules. It flags negation-scope, medication, numeric/unit and medication-dose binding conflicts as review-required; it always keeps automatic adoption disabled and states that candidate agreement does not verify clinical truth. Mechanistic synthetic tests cover scope movement and aspirin/amlodipine dose swaps; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 5 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this comparison is rule-based, not clinically validated, and is not yet connected to every candidate workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E10:** Extended correction-suggestion records to require a source audio ID and non-empty rationale, and to retain both original and proposed text with `human_review_state=pending`, `reviewed_by=null`, and `adopted=false`. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. References are upstream TextGrid labels and optimal scoring mappings are not role confirmations. No VAD-turn diarization arm is included, so the requested three-way modality comparison is incomplete; clinical speaker accuracy is not claimed. - **MTA-ASR-G06:** Existing subgroup report `evaluation/reports/asr-subgroups-v1.json` (SHA-256 3d65850d0248a9ff516a51baf53ea8a3dd610b7a861e9d29a80ec0c653c67852) disaggregates overlap status, reference role and turn length; segmentation diagnostics separately mark omitted short turns and boundary clipping. tests/test_asr_subgroup_diagnostics.py and test_asr_segmentation.py: 13 passed; Ruff passes. Status: partial; upstream mock annotations are not adjudicated, and no standalone overlap detector or validated missed-short- patient-turn rate has been established. - **MTA-ASR-G07:** Existing `SpeakerRoles` UI provides audio preview and explicit role assignment; the API requires clinician confirmation and `If-Match` against the current transcript before creating a new version. UI and backend preserve the historical source versions. Status: partial; reviewers cannot yet split, merge or reassign individual turns between anonymous speaker clusters, and a complete stale-note invalidation workflow has not been verified end to end for these edits. - **MTA-ASR-G08:** Existing failure-inclusive subgroup reports separate patient and clinician reference-role edits; the detailed development run preserves unknown roles rather than coercing them. Status: partial; no patient-prioritized runtime quality control or medically critical patient omission measure is wired, and upstream role annotations are not independently adjudicated. - **MTA-ASR-G09:** Existing transcript outputs remain `review_required`, carry `speaker_unassigned`/unconfirmed role flags, and mark timing gaps as untranscribed with unknown cause. Role-dependent fact checks require confirmation or block approval rather than moving evidence across speakers. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. Current HTTP-to-worker integration tests exercise crop, cancellation, resource contention and candidate publication using generated fixtures/stub adapters; public-audio benchmark runs are separate offline evaluation jobs. The full real-worker matrix across mono/stereo, silence, clipping, crosstalk and interrupted model inference has not been executed, so no real-worker speaker/timing accuracy claim is made. - **MTA-ASR-H01:** Partial. `docs/device-profile.md` defines one x86 CPU workstation with at least four threads and 16 GB RAM, without an assumed GPU. The frozen detailed set contains eight unique consultation groups across 16 paired clean/noisy recordings (1.32 recorded hours, with shared source content across conditions); labels are upstream mock references and are not independently adjudicated. This supports offline inference experiments, not training a speech foundation model from scratch. A credible FLOP/time estimate is unavailable without a selected architecture and measured training throughput; no from-scratch training is claimed or attempted. - **MTA-ASR-H02:** Partial. Current benchmark source manifests and local model profiles bind dataset/model revisions and license identifiers; lexicon construction further requires rights-reviewed development manifests and verified locks. No gated or restricted model/data was used in the reported local runs, and no derived training artifact exists. This is a preflight for the evaluated assets, not authorization to train on any additional source; each future training input and derived artifact needs its own rights review. - **MTA-ASR-H03:** Partial. Development manifests identify consultation-group IDs, and `evaluation/acceptance-reservation-v1.json` reserves three groups before inference for future independent annotation. Current evaluation uses development groups only; there is no training split or training manifest because no adaptation has been run. Group separation does not prove speaker, site, device or model-training independence, and no shared-speaker leakage check is possible from the available metadata. - **MTA-ASR-H04:** Not run. No training augmentation artifacts were generated. Existing gain/filter/noise-suppression work is paired inference-time signal processing with source provenance; it is not relabeled training data or a training augmentation gain. Any future licensed development augmentation needs reproducible seeds, parent/derived hashes and label-preservation checks. - **MTA-ASR-H05:** Not run. Existing ROVER and hotword experiments are inference-time candidate generation/decoding comparisons, not trained correction or reranking components. No cross-fitted training table was created; reserved acceptance groups remain excluded. A future confusion table would need group-level train/development boundaries and source-linked labels before any component is fit. - **MTA-ASR-H06:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. Existing inference profiles provide converted/quantized decoder artifacts, not an approved training architecture, optimizer recipe or adapter checkpoint. The reference host has CPU-only capacity and no qualified training accelerator; no LoRA/rescoring training has been simulated or claimed. - **MTA-ASR-H07:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No candidate has genuine calibrated acoustic scores or a disjoint group-level calibration corpus; current backend confidence is explicitly unsupported. F09 records the same evidence gap. No reliability curves or selection thresholds are fabricated. - **MTA-ASR-H08:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No independently verified clinician-confirmed correction set is available. Existing UI edits are source-versioned operational corrections, not research training labels; synthetic fixtures and developer-authored proposals are never treated as clinician signatures or automatic self-training input. - **MTA-ASR-H09:** Not implemented. There is no training/adapter corpus or clinician-correction lexicon state to remove, and no future-training lineage deletion mechanism has been tested. Current E01 lexicon entries bind to licensed development-manifest digests and are write-once artifacts; that provenance is not equivalent to revocation/unlearning propagation. - **MTA-ASR-H10:** No adaptation-attributable gain is established (`null`). No correction model, LoRA adapter or rescoring model was trained. The E08 hotword pilot changes decoding only and worsened aggregate WER on its small matched subset; it cannot be credited as an adaptation gain. - **MTA-ASR-I01:** Partial. `evaluation/selection-policy.json` and frozen evaluation contracts predeclare failure-inclusive normalized WER and retain the unchanged <=5% ceiling; existing reports cannot weaken it. Clinical critical-error and patient-role non-inferiority tolerances are still pending a clinical owner, and no independent adjudicated acceptance set is available. The primary WER endpoint is frozen, but the safety-gate preregistration is incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I02:** Partial. Existing frozen reports provide identical-input comparisons for fixed/overlap/speech-aware/context segmentation and for matched decoder/consensus arms; the E08 term-bias pilot also pairs baseline and biased decoding on identical crops. The full declared matrix (VAD-only, terminology-only, repair-only and full pipeline under equal compute) has not been run on one frozen cohort, so no end-to-end method attribution is claimed. - **MTA-ASR-I03:** `FAIL` for every currently evaluated model/system profile. The unchanged admission ceiling is normalized WER <=5%; the best expanded short-clip model result is still 8.70%, and full-consultation/detailed runs are worse. D10's gate remains fail-closed and no inference-mode promotion is allowed. Relative improvement does not change this result. - **MTA-ASR-I04:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. The admission policy requires separate critical insertion/substitution/omission and role-safety review, but no independently adjudicated clinical annotations or owner-approved tolerances are available. The E08 pilot's false insertion is a development signal, not a clinical error rate. Abstentions remain review-required and cannot be counted as successful corrections. - **MTA-ASR-I05:** Engineering system path is now exercised by `tests/test_real_local_asr_workflow.py`: the existing licensed PriMock57 patient utterance passes through upload, PCM ingest, the actual locally installed tiny.en Faster Whisper model, immutable native-timestamped transcript, versioned source review, note verification, approval and integrity-checked JSON export. The test passed against the current local model artifacts. Review and approval actions are scripted for this public mock fixture; they do not represent clinician review, clinical validity or user acceptance. The frozen WER and independent safety gates remain separate. - **MTA-ASR-I06:** Partial. High-risk medication, dose/unit, negation and allergy edits are emitted as pending, non-adopted suggestions while original ASR text remains intact (`tests/test_asr_postprocess.py`: 5 passed). Transcript edits create immutable child versions and stale approvals fail closed; span retranscription checks bind to the current source/audio. This is software guard coverage only: the broader review/retranscription workflow test command did not finish in this run, and coverage does not establish clinician review quality. No automatic adoption path was found in these reviewed correction modules. - **MTA-ASR-I07:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/paired-asr-bootstrap-v1.json` reports paired clean-versus-distracted WER deltas using consultation-level resampling (10,000 deterministic iterations, 95% percentile intervals) and records both arms and failed statuses for each pair. It is a development-only convenience sample. The report does not stratify paired uncertainty by clinical term or speaker, and preserved failure statuses are not adjudicated clinical error estimates; the requested full uncertainty analysis remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I08:** Partial. Existing compute Pareto receipts report measured case wall time and RTF percentiles for selected inference profiles; worker receipts also retain per-job wall time. The Pareto report explicitly leaves ASR peak memory unknown, and no end-to-end successfully completed consultation cost (including resource amortization) is measured. These profile-level inference timings do not satisfy the requested full consultation metrics. - **MTA-ASR-I09:** Partial. Model cards and a negative-experiment index exist, and benchmark receipts bind runs to dataset/model/source digests. However, the index is a bounded historical inventory and the reporting artifacts do not currently provide one reproducible publication package with every requested ablation/error table regenerated from source-bound receipts. Clinical-gold and admission claims remain explicitly absent. - **MTA-ASR-I10:** Partial. Synthetic tests cover digital-silence hallucination rejection, cross-talk detection, repeated-token stitching integrity, and source/candidate safety guards. `tests/test_adversarial_cases.py` records only synthetic cases and explicitly has no clinical gold. There is no complete audio-level suite for low-volume patient denial, deceptive spoken prompts and corrupt media through the real ASR worker; resulting-note non-approval is therefore not established across the requested challenge set. - **MTA-ASR-I12:** Defined in `evaluation/asr-capability-matrix-v1.json`. It distinguishes verified local CPU profiles, conditional/unqualified CUDA profiles, and missing/corrupt weights (unavailable, no automatic download). All rows preserve the independent clinical/WER admission gate. CUDA remains a conditional statement, not a hardware validation result. - **MTA-ASR-I11:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` for the requested release check. The repository CI workflow declares Python quality/full-suite, frontend, PostgreSQL and container jobs, but GitHub returned no status checks for the current source commit `8d93b88f4a170d12e2e64a7b28a3ae23e1fb9060`. The latest available local acceptance receipt is from an earlier source commit and records a timed-out full backend run plus missing PyAV, PostgreSQL DSN and Docker. Those results are not promoted as exact-HEAD evidence; all required exact-HEAD CI lanes remain unverified. - **MTA-ASR-I13:** Partial. The clinician source-review screen supports keyboard-operated source-interval playback, transcript text edits, and saving corrections as a new version. The read-only ASR error-review packet shows waveform clips/audio, source intervals and candidate alternatives, but is a research/development tool, not the clinician queue. The clinician screen does not present reason-coded ASR alternatives as an uncertain-span queue, and no scripted usability acceptance was run for that workflow. - **MTA-ASR-I14:** Published `evaluation/reports/asr-objective-release-v1.json` with objective-level `FAIL`/`BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` decisions for model qualification, clinical safety, end-to-end product acceptance and engineering CI. Missing evidence is never treated as PASS; the report authorizes no model promotion or clinical use. - **MTA-ASR-I13 update:** Implemented a clinician-facing uncertain-span queue in the source review screen. It lists original transcript text, known uncertainty reasons, supplied alternatives when present, and untranscribed source intervals; keyboard activation seeks to the source and focuses its versioned editor. TypeScript and the production build pass. The browser usability test could not navigate to the local test server (`ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED`), and current ASR profiles do not supply alternate hypotheses or a rendered waveform, so full I13 acceptance remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I05 update:** A separate invocation through the pinned tiny.en adapter on the locked PriMock57 patient smoke clip succeeded, produced two native-timestamped segments, and reported 1.33 seconds inference time after model load. This is real model evidence but not a full system run. These profile-level inference timings do not satisfy the requested full consultation metrics. - **MTA-ASR-I09:** Partial. Model cards and a negative-experiment index exist, and benchmark receipts bind runs to dataset/model/source digests. However, the index is a bounded historical inventory and the reporting artifacts do not currently provide one reproducible publication package with every requested ablation/error table regenerated from source-bound receipts. Clinical-gold and admission claims remain explicitly absent. - **MTA-ASR-I10:** Partial. Synthetic tests cover digital-silence hallucination rejection, cross-talk detection, repeated-token stitching integrity, and source/candidate safety guards. `tests/test_adversarial_cases.py` records only synthetic cases and explicitly has no clinical gold. There is no complete audio-level suite for low-volume patient denial, deceptive spoken prompts and corrupt media through the real ASR worker; resulting-note non-approval is therefore not established across the requested challenge set. - **MTA-ASR-I12:** Defined in `evaluation/asr-capability-matrix-v1.json`. It distinguishes verified local CPU profiles, conditional/unqualified CUDA profiles, and missing/corrupt weights (unavailable, no automatic download). All rows preserve the independent clinical/WER admission gate. CUDA remains a conditional statement, not a hardware validation result. - **MTA-ASR-I11:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` for the requested release check. The repository CI workflow declares Python quality/full-suite, frontend, PostgreSQL and container jobs, but GitHub returned no status checks for the current source commit `8d93b88f4a170d12e2e64a7b28a3ae23e1fb9060`. The latest available local acceptance receipt is from an earlier source commit and records a timed-out full backend run plus missing PyAV, PostgreSQL DSN and Docker. Those results are not promoted as exact-HEAD evidence; all required exact-HEAD CI lanes remain unverified. - **MTA-ASR-I13:** Partial. The clinician source-review screen supports keyboard-operated source-interval playback, transcript text edits, and saving corrections as a new version. The read-only ASR error-review packet shows waveform clips/audio, source intervals and candidate alternatives, but is a research/development tool, not the clinician queue. The clinician screen does not present reason-coded ASR alternatives as an uncertain-span queue, and no scripted usability acceptance was run for that workflow. - **MTA-ASR-I14:** Published `evaluation/reports/asr-objective-release-v1.json` with objective-level `FAIL`/`BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` decisions for model qualification, clinical safety, end-to-end product acceptance and engineering CI. Missing evidence is never treated as PASS; the report authorizes no model promotion or clinical use. - **MTA-ASR-I13 update:** Implemented a clinician-facing uncertain-span queue in the source review screen. It lists original transcript text, known uncertainty reasons, supplied alternatives when present, and untranscribed source intervals; keyboard activation seeks to the source and focuses its versioned editor. TypeScript and the production build pass. The browser usability test could not navigate to the local test server (`ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED`), and current ASR profiles do not supply alternate hypotheses or a rendered waveform, so full I13 acceptance remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I05 update:** A separate invocation through the pinned tiny.en adapter on the locked PriMock57 patient smoke clip succeeded, produced two native-timestamped segments, and reported 1.33 seconds inference time after model load. This is real model evidence but not a full system run. The local application-test harness stalls on its first in-process HTTP request even for the pre-existing synthetic transcription workflow; the added integration attempt was removed rather than retaining a hanging test. The full audio-to-approved-export acceptance remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I05 integration update:** The prior transport stall was traced to the sandbox denying the Windows asyncio loopback socket used by Starlette's `TestClient`; it was not an application-route deadlock. With permitted loopback for the isolated test, the new real-model workflow test completed audio upload through integrity-checked approved export (1 passed). This is reproducible engineering-path evidence only: the review/approval actions are scripted and do not close independent clinical acceptance. - **MTA-ASR-I13 waveform update:** The clinician uncertain-span queue now renders source-bound waveform peaks and highlights each selected transcript or untranscribed interval. The authenticated API checks the stored audio hash and returns at most 160 amplitude bins, optionally for a selected channel; the browser does not decode a full recording into memory. The production frontend build and tests/test_audio_waveform.py pass, and apps/clinician-web/e2e/uncertain-span-waveform.spec.ts passed against the isolated synthetic browser fixture. I13 remains partial because the installed ASR backends do not provide alternate hypotheses; no alternatives are invented. - **MTA-ASR-I14 update:** Published evaluation/reports/asr-objective-release-v3.json, source-bound to commit e5da4cd5258d25cd6ffe908eeb3cb81f73d9b113. It adds the waveform browser evidence while retaining FAIL for model qualification and product acceptance, and BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE for clinical safety and exact-HEAD release CI. Versions v1 and v2 remain preserved. - **MTA-ASR-I14 update:** Published evaluation/reports/asr-objective-release-v2.json, source-bound to commit cf538fc33a1975121af7add8ee70438aca87c561. It records the real-model engineering-path result while retaining FAIL for product acceptance and model qualification, and BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE for clinical safety and exact-HEAD release CI. The earlier v1 decision remains preserved. - **MTA-ASR-C02:** Verified and regression-pinned the current full-consultation fixed-window baseline before further segmentation claims. The source-bound ranking identifies `omi-med-stt-v1-native-empty` first at 16.41% clean / 17.22% distracted WER. Its matched overlap and speech-aware arms score worse in both conditions; each arm has 8 foregrounds, 13,683 reference words and zero failed samples. `tests/test_fixed_window_baseline.py`: 1 passed; it checks exact report hashes, manifest/suite bindings, common denominators, and the unchanged 5% gate. This confirms only the development baseline; every arm still fails admission, and it does not qualify Omi for clinical use. - **MTA-ASR-C10:** Partial and still open. The existing large-v3 speech-aware receipt contains 14/16 records (7 clean, 7 distracted) and is explicitly `complete: false`; both records for `day1_consultation08` are missing. Its measured completed cases consumed about 14,217 seconds of inference, before model loading. The runner supports hash-validated resume, but completing the remaining full-consultation arms requires a sustained benchmark run. No missing samples are imputed and no C10 completion claim is made. Peak RAM is also absent from the historical mode receipts, so it must be measured in any accepted rerun. - **MTA-ASR-D01:** The operational application path remains the pinned Faster Whisper 1.2.1 adapter. `ASRProfile` freezes decoder configuration (`beam_size=5`, English, CPU INT8 by default), profile/artifact hashes are included in runtime receipts, and the adapter uses deterministic decoding options (`temperature=0`, VAD off, no previous-text conditioning). The backend contract regression checks native segment timestamps, profile hash, and unsupported confidence. No alternate decoder was promoted. This records the preserved contract; exact deployment profile regressions still need to run on the target deployment host. - **MTA-ASR-D05:** Partial. The pinned Faster Whisper adapter now preserves its native winning-sequence token IDs and segment average log probability in the immutable transcript. The receipt explicitly labels this as one-best decoder evidence, with n_best_supported=false and calibrated=false; it is not a confidence estimate. Omi and Parakeet continue to declare n-best/confidence unsupported. Backend and transcript regressions validate native meaning and reject invalid scores; see tests/test_asr_decoder_evidence.py and tests/test_asr_optional_runtime_dependencies.py. Multiple hypotheses and calibrated uncertainty remain unavailable. - **MTA-ASR-I15:** Research summary and paper section are present in `docs/asr-rnd-research-section.md`, covering the hypothesis, method, baselines, negative findings, novelty limits, ablation gaps, ethics and reproducibility pointers. No novel clinical acoustic reranking claim is made; related-work comparison and the full matched-compute ablation matrix remain open.

tasks.requirement: Implement join-stitching using stable segment IDs, window offsets and deduplication of overlapped tokens. **
tasks.acceptance: ** Synthetic repeated-edge words remain once when appropriate, and true repetitions remain intact.

progress_evidence.text: - **MTA-ASR-C04:** Added stitching that requires one output per stable segment ID, orders by source offsets, and deduplicates exact suffix/prefix tokens only when the windows overlap. Every removal is marked for audio review; non-overlapping repeated words are preserved. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py covers repeated edges, true non-overlap repetitions, and missing outputs. Status: partial; no measured word timestamps exist to disambiguate a true repeated word that happens at an overlapping window edge. - **MTA-ASR-C05:** Added tunable VAD candidate minimum duration, maximum duration, and padding, preserving source sample offsets and checking supplied speech-span coverage. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py exercises short-span padding, duration limits, and coverage failures. Status: partial; thresholds have not been ablated against matched frozen conversations. - **MTA-ASR-C06:** Added source-span diagnostics for omitted short turns, window-edge clips, partial coverage, joined known roles, and windows carrying unknown-role turns. tests/test_asr_segmentation.py verifies each category. Status: partial; no annotated conversation audio is available to generate measured boundary reports. - **MTA-ASR-C09:** Added inverse source-frame/window-frame mapping keyed by stable window ID, returning channel identity where applicable. Round-trip tests cover fixed crops and channel-first windows. Status: partial; the helper covers same-rate sample-index crops; resampled audio must use the separate measured-delay mapping contract, and runtime transcript integration remains pending. - **MTA-ASR-C08:** Added regression cases for exact shared suffix/prefix, backtracking around a shared medical phrase, and repeated metformin mentions in an overlap. tests/test_overlap_stitch_integrity.py exercises the existing sequence-alignment reassembler. Status: partial; alignment remains hypothesis-text-only and ambiguous repeated edge speech still requires original-audio review. - **MTA-ASR-C07:** Added bounded context handoff requiring an explicitly acoustically reviewed prior span and a current candidate-speech signal; silent or indeterminate current windows receive empty context. Tests verify bounded carryover and silence suppression. Status: partial; this contract is not yet wired into a long-form decoder, and candidate activity is a VAD heuristic rather than proof of speech. - **MTA-ASR-D02:** Added a typed ASR backend contract for inference, availability, timestamp capability, n-best capability, confidence capability, and runtime receipts. The faster-whisper adapter declares segment timestamps and explicitly unsupported n-best/confidence. Fake provider tests cover missing models, timeout exceptions, malformed output, and capability honesty. Status: partial; timeout propagation is tested as a provider failure, but no hard cancellation of a non-cooperative backend is implemented. - **MTA-ASR-D03:** Added an Omi backend candidate wrapper that requires the exact local GGUF digest, pinned runtime and existing CPU library; automatic downloads are disabled. It reports text-only output with no native timestamps, n-best, or confidence. Added tests/test_omi_backend.py for rejecting missing weights before runtime initialization. Status: partial; the focused pytest process stalled before collection and did not complete, and no production worker profile or inference-mode promotion is configured. - **MTA-ASR-D06:** Added normalized pairwise transcript disagreement with differing token spans. The output states that scores are uncalibrated, agreement is not truth, and no candidate selection occurs. tests/test_hypothesis_disagreement.py covers negation, dose substitution, agreement, and invalid candidate sets. Status: partial; thresholds have not been tuned against labeled disagreement cases and the diagnostic is not wired into runtime routing. Ruff and a direct substitution smoke check pass; focused pytest stalled before collection in this environment. - **MTA-ASR-D10:** Added a fail-closed candidate admission gate that requires failure-inclusive WER at or below the unchanged 5% maximum, validated source timing, reviewed licensing, passed critical-safety review, and matched evaluation. Tests cover exact gate boundary and each denial reason. Status: partial; no deployment promotion command is wired to this policy, so current profiles remain explicitly not admitted. - **MTA-ASR-D07:** Implemented and ran a post-hoc ROVER-style confusion-network vote on three frozen fixed-window engines over the same 16 consultation cases. Report evaluation/reports/rover-meddistract-detailed-v2-final.json SHA-256 4a47684f4b148bc57e8ce0bdde18665a108dfbc51e8cf39a3fae0063174b3f93 binds all source report hashes, model configuration digests, the frozen suite, and the ROVER/scorer code hashes. ROVER: 5,617/27,366 edits (20.525%); faster-whisper large-v3: 5,798 (21.187%); Parakeet: 6,071 (22.184%); Omi: 7,708 (28.166%). Two Omi failures are retained and mark those ROVER cases failed. tests/test_rover.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this unweighted voting baseline remains far above the 5% gate and has no clinical critical-token validation or inference-mode promotion. - **MTA-ASR-D08:** Added a sequential backend pool that closes the active model before loading another, serializes requests, and fails closed on lock timeout or MemoryError. Its receipt explicitly says memory admission was not measured. Tests cover switching, contention, and resource failure. Status: partial; the pool is not wired into the application worker and no full-process memory or 16 GB hardware admission test has been run. - **MTA-ASR-D09:** Generated a matched single/two-engine Pareto report from the frozen 16-case detailed runs. evaluation/reports/asr-compute-pareto-v1.json SHA-256 E909202756CF5D0F5383A9D81A14F3F86FA86F99878913C73EB82C7AA257B62C binds report, suite, model configuration, and code hashes. Single-engine p95 case wall RTFs: faster-whisper large-v3 2.082, Omi 0.294, Parakeet 0.106. Sequential faster-whisper plus Parakeet p95 RTF: 2.186. Two-engine WER equals the faster-whisper pivot because two-way token ties favor pivot; all arms fail the 5% gate. Peak ASR memory and CPU seconds are explicitly unknown; targeted fallback was not evaluated. tests/test_asr_pareto.py: 2 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; fresh resource measurements and a targeted-fallback arm remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-D04:** Added a Parakeet ONNX backend implementing the common backend contract. It verifies the exact local artifact set and digests, requires onnx-asr 0.12.0, uses CPU execution, disables downloads, and declares text-only output without timestamps or confidence. Tests cover missing weights and truthful capability receipts. Status: partial; although frozen Parakeet benchmark outputs exist, this new adapter is not integrated into application selected-window routing. - **MTA-ASR-E01:** Added a reproducible, provenance-bound English lexicon candidate artifact at evaluation/lexicons/clinical-english-v1-e01.json (SHA-256 af4b321287acd7762f6a9f63fe1ca29c4fc71ce0c52eda0ef95288efbfa4d142). The builder accepts only rights-reviewed, locked development manifests, rejects reserved acceptance groups, excludes uncertain reference rows, and records record/group IDs, reference hashes, offsets and dataset/manifest digests for each occurrence. It found one seed term (paracetamol) in eight licensed development references. tests/test_clinical_lexicon.py: 2 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the seed inventory is only the existing five generic opt-in hints, this artifact does not validate clinical terminology, and no backend consumes it for decoding or reranking. - **MTA-ASR-E02:** Added strict, immutable ASR clinical-entity schema kinds for drug name, strength, route, frequency, allergy, negation, anatomy, measurement and temporal relation. The current deterministic extractor emits only source-spanned medication and strength candidates, binds each strength to a medication, and keeps simple negated/uncertain clause status explicit. Tests disambiguate aspirin 75 mg from amlodipine 5 mg and a denied drug from an affirmed one; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this heuristic covers only simple English clauses, is not clinically validated, and does not yet emit the other declared entity types or route/frequency relations. - **MTA-ASR-E03:** Hardened the non-destructive ASR suggestion path. It now preserves a deep copy of raw segments, retains original text beside each proposal, marks every proposal review-required and non-adopted, and emits explicit reasons when medication identities or numeric/unit signatures differ. Invalid suggestion indexes fail closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this safeguards the helper contract, but the postprocessor is not yet the sole publication path for every runtime transcript workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E04:** Wired the pinned faster-whisper `hotwords` decoder hook to an optional, hash-pinned lexicon selection. Only terms present in the E01 provenance artifact are accepted; the adapter records candidate-only bias metadata and does not mutate text. The official faster-whisper interface documents `hotwords` as a decode hint. Focused adapter/context tests: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this permits only the single term currently present in the lexicon, and no paired bias/no-bias WER or false-insertion evaluation has been run, so it is not an admitted profile. - **MTA-ASR-E05:** Partial, resource-limited. The existing synthetic ASR challenge lists a generic `medical_homophone` case but contains no reviewed drug-name confusable pairs or clinical gold. The licensed development lexicon currently has one observed term, so it cannot support a meaningful sound-alike/abbreviation subgroup evaluation. Existing medication-binding checks cover explicit medication and dose swaps, but are not phonetic confusability evidence. No clinical correctness claim is made; completion requires an approved, rights-reviewed confusable set and reference labels. - **MTA-ASR-E09:** Partial, metadata-limited. Audited the six frozen development dataset manifests; none declares accent/dialect labels. No accent subgroups or accent identity were inferred from audio or names. Accordingly no accent-related accuracy result is reported. Completion requires legally available English mock data with actual reviewed metadata and a sufficient matched denominator. - **MTA-ASR-E06:** Added a finite candidate formatter limited to whitespace and case normalization for recognized numbers with supported explicit units. It verifies the before/after quantity signature, preserves the original string, never adds a missing unit, and never automatically adopts a candidate. Tests cover decimal/unit distinctions and unsupported or absent units; tests/test_asr_number_format.py: 3 passed and postprocess controls: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no additional unit systems or app publication integration are claimed. - **MTA-ASR-E08:** Ran a paired local faster-whisper tiny.en development pilot on four clean paracetamol-positive turns and four nearest non-target turns. evaluation/reports/asr-lexicon-bias-pilot-v1-final.json SHA-256 d2fa02f5c7a894a8cdd57c7a6bd99136241aa1350c6b86cdd60e0150f0b616a7 binds the frozen dataset/lock, profile, lexicon and evaluator/adapter code hashes. Exact-term recall changed 1/4 to 4/4, while false insertions changed 0/4 to 1/4 and normalized WER worsened from 44/153 (28.76%) to 46/153 (30.07%); no inference failures occurred. The result is development-only, not adjudicated clinical gold. Status: partial; this small pilot shows a non-target insertion and worse overall WER, and cannot justify enabling biasing or satisfy full-cohort validation. - **MTA-ASR-E07:** Added an ASR candidate comparison wrapper around the conservative source-vs-claim rules. It flags negation-scope, medication, numeric/unit and medication-dose binding conflicts as review-required; it always keeps automatic adoption disabled and states that candidate agreement does not verify clinical truth. Mechanistic synthetic tests cover scope movement and aspirin/amlodipine dose swaps; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 5 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this comparison is rule-based, not clinically validated, and is not yet connected to every candidate workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E10:** Extended correction-suggestion records to require a source audio ID and non-empty rationale, and to retain both original and proposed text with `human_review_state=pending`, `reviewed_by=null`, and `adopted=false`. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. References are upstream TextGrid labels and optimal scoring mappings are not role confirmations. No VAD-turn diarization arm is included, so the requested three-way modality comparison is incomplete; clinical speaker accuracy is not claimed. - **MTA-ASR-G06:** Existing subgroup report `evaluation/reports/asr-subgroups-v1.json` (SHA-256 3d65850d0248a9ff516a51baf53ea8a3dd610b7a861e9d29a80ec0c653c67852) disaggregates overlap status, reference role and turn length; segmentation diagnostics separately mark omitted short turns and boundary clipping. tests/test_asr_subgroup_diagnostics.py and test_asr_segmentation.py: 13 passed; Ruff passes. Status: partial; upstream mock annotations are not adjudicated, and no standalone overlap detector or validated missed-short- patient-turn rate has been established. - **MTA-ASR-G07:** Existing `SpeakerRoles` UI provides audio preview and explicit role assignment; the API requires clinician confirmation and `If-Match` against the current transcript before creating a new version. UI and backend preserve the historical source versions. Status: partial; reviewers cannot yet split, merge or reassign individual turns between anonymous speaker clusters, and a complete stale-note invalidation workflow has not been verified end to end for these edits. - **MTA-ASR-G08:** Existing failure-inclusive subgroup reports separate patient and clinician reference-role edits; the detailed development run preserves unknown roles rather than coercing them. Status: partial; no patient-prioritized runtime quality control or medically critical patient omission measure is wired, and upstream role annotations are not independently adjudicated. - **MTA-ASR-G09:** Existing transcript outputs remain `review_required`, carry `speaker_unassigned`/unconfirmed role flags, and mark timing gaps as untranscribed with unknown cause. Role-dependent fact checks require confirmation or block approval rather than moving evidence across speakers. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. Current HTTP-to-worker integration tests exercise crop, cancellation, resource contention and candidate publication using generated fixtures/stub adapters; public-audio benchmark runs are separate offline evaluation jobs. The full real-worker matrix across mono/stereo, silence, clipping, crosstalk and interrupted model inference has not been executed, so no real-worker speaker/timing accuracy claim is made. - **MTA-ASR-H01:** Partial. `docs/device-profile.md` defines one x86 CPU workstation with at least four threads and 16 GB RAM, without an assumed GPU. The frozen detailed set contains eight unique consultation groups across 16 paired clean/noisy recordings (1.32 recorded hours, with shared source content across conditions); labels are upstream mock references and are not independently adjudicated. This supports offline inference experiments, not training a speech foundation model from scratch. A credible FLOP/time estimate is unavailable without a selected architecture and measured training throughput; no from-scratch training is claimed or attempted. - **MTA-ASR-H02:** Partial. Current benchmark source manifests and local model profiles bind dataset/model revisions and license identifiers; lexicon construction further requires rights-reviewed development manifests and verified locks. No gated or restricted model/data was used in the reported local runs, and no derived training artifact exists. This is a preflight for the evaluated assets, not authorization to train on any additional source; each future training input and derived artifact needs its own rights review. - **MTA-ASR-H03:** Partial. Development manifests identify consultation-group IDs, and `evaluation/acceptance-reservation-v1.json` reserves three groups before inference for future independent annotation. Current evaluation uses development groups only; there is no training split or training manifest because no adaptation has been run. Group separation does not prove speaker, site, device or model-training independence, and no shared-speaker leakage check is possible from the available metadata. - **MTA-ASR-H04:** Not run. No training augmentation artifacts were generated. Existing gain/filter/noise-suppression work is paired inference-time signal processing with source provenance; it is not relabeled training data or a training augmentation gain. Any future licensed development augmentation needs reproducible seeds, parent/derived hashes and label-preservation checks. - **MTA-ASR-H05:** Not run. Existing ROVER and hotword experiments are inference-time candidate generation/decoding comparisons, not trained correction or reranking components. No cross-fitted training table was created; reserved acceptance groups remain excluded. A future confusion table would need group-level train/development boundaries and source-linked labels before any component is fit. - **MTA-ASR-H06:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. Existing inference profiles provide converted/quantized decoder artifacts, not an approved training architecture, optimizer recipe or adapter checkpoint. The reference host has CPU-only capacity and no qualified training accelerator; no LoRA/rescoring training has been simulated or claimed. - **MTA-ASR-H07:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No candidate has genuine calibrated acoustic scores or a disjoint group-level calibration corpus; current backend confidence is explicitly unsupported. F09 records the same evidence gap. No reliability curves or selection thresholds are fabricated. - **MTA-ASR-H08:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No independently verified clinician-confirmed correction set is available. Existing UI edits are source-versioned operational corrections, not research training labels; synthetic fixtures and developer-authored proposals are never treated as clinician signatures or automatic self-training input. - **MTA-ASR-H09:** Not implemented. There is no training/adapter corpus or clinician-correction lexicon state to remove, and no future-training lineage deletion mechanism has been tested.
