progress_evidence.status_basis: Added strict, immutable ASR clinical-entity schema kinds for drug name, strength, route, frequency, allergy, negation, anatomy, measurement and temporal relation. The current deterministic extractor emits only source-spanned medication and strength candidates, binds each strength to a medication, and keeps simple negated/uncertain clause status explicit. Tests disambiguate aspirin 75 mg from amlodipine 5 mg and a denied drug from an affirmed one; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this heuristic covers only simple English clauses, is not clinically validated, and does not yet emit the other declared entity types or route/frequency relations. - **MTA-ASR-E03:** Hardened the non-destructive ASR suggestion path. It now preserves a deep copy of raw segments, retains original text beside each proposal, marks every proposal review-required and non-adopted, and emits explicit reasons when medication identities or numeric/unit signatures differ. Invalid suggestion indexes fail closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this safeguards the helper contract, but the postprocessor is not yet the sole publication path for every runtime transcript workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E04:** Wired the pinned faster-whisper `hotwords` decoder hook to an optional, hash-pinned lexicon selection. Only terms present in the E01 provenance artifact are accepted; the adapter records candidate-only bias metadata and does not mutate text. The official faster-whisper interface documents `hotwords` as a decode hint. Focused adapter/context tests: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this permits only the single term currently present in the lexicon, and no paired bias/no-bias WER or false-insertion evaluation has been run, so it is not an admitted profile. - **MTA-ASR-E05:** Partial, resource-limited. The existing synthetic ASR challenge lists a generic `medical_homophone` case but contains no reviewed drug-name confusable pairs or clinical gold. The licensed development lexicon currently has one observed term, so it cannot support a meaningful sound-alike/abbreviation subgroup evaluation. Existing medication-binding checks cover explicit medication and dose swaps, but are not phonetic confusability evidence. No clinical correctness claim is made; completion requires an approved, rights-reviewed confusable set and reference labels. - **MTA-ASR-E09:** Partial, metadata-limited. Audited the six frozen development dataset manifests; none declares accent/dialect labels. No accent subgroups or accent identity were inferred from audio or names. Accordingly no accent-related accuracy result is reported. Completion requires legally available English mock data with actual reviewed metadata and a sufficient matched denominator. - **MTA-ASR-E06:** Added a finite candidate formatter limited to whitespace and case normalization for recognized numbers with supported explicit units. It verifies the before/after quantity signature, preserves the original string, never adds a missing unit, and never automatically adopts a candidate. Tests cover decimal/unit distinctions and unsupported or absent units; tests/test_asr_number_format.py: 3 passed and postprocess controls: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no additional unit systems or app publication integration are claimed. - **MTA-ASR-E08:** Ran a paired local faster-whisper tiny.en development pilot on four clean paracetamol-positive turns and four nearest non-target turns. evaluation/reports/asr-lexicon-bias-pilot-v1-final.json SHA-256 d2fa02f5c7a894a8cdd57c7a6bd99136241aa1350c6b86cdd60e0150f0b616a7 binds the frozen dataset/lock, profile, lexicon and evaluator/adapter code hashes. Exact-term recall changed 1/4 to 4/4, while false insertions changed 0/4 to 1/4 and normalized WER worsened from 44/153 (28.76%) to 46/153 (30.07%); no inference failures occurred. The result is development-only, not adjudicated clinical gold. Status: partial; this small pilot shows a non-target insertion and worse overall WER, and cannot justify enabling biasing or satisfy full-cohort validation. - **MTA-ASR-E07:** Added an ASR candidate comparison wrapper around the conservative source-vs-claim rules. It flags negation-scope, medication, numeric/unit and medication-dose binding conflicts as review-required; it always keeps automatic adoption disabled and states that candidate agreement does not verify clinical truth. Mechanistic synthetic tests cover scope movement and aspirin/amlodipine dose swaps; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 5 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this comparison is rule-based, not clinically validated, and is not yet connected to every candidate workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E10:** Extended correction-suggestion records to require a source audio ID and non-empty rationale, and to retain both original and proposed text with `human_review_state=pending`, `reviewed_by=null`, and `adopted=false`. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. High-risk medication, dose/unit, negation and allergy edits are emitted as pending, non-adopted suggestions while original ASR text remains intact (`tests/test_asr_postprocess.py`: 5 passed). This is software guard coverage only: the broader review/retranscription workflow test command did not finish in this run, and coverage does not establish clinician review quality. It is a development-only convenience sample. The report does not stratify paired uncertainty by clinical term or speaker, and preserved failure statuses are not adjudicated clinical error estimates; the requested full uncertainty analysis remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I08:** Partial. Existing compute Pareto receipts report measured case wall time and RTF percentiles for selected inference profiles; worker receipts also retain per-job wall time. The Pareto report explicitly leaves ASR peak memory unknown, and no end-to-end successfully completed consultation cost (including resource amortization) is measured. These profile-level inference timings do not satisfy the requested full consultation metrics. - **MTA-ASR-I09:** Partial. Model cards and a negative-experiment index exist, and benchmark receipts bind runs to dataset/model/source digests. However, the index is a bounded historical inventory and the reporting artifacts do not currently provide one reproducible publication package with every requested ablation/error table regenerated from source-bound receipts. Clinical-gold and admission claims remain explicitly absent. - **MTA-ASR-I10:** Partial. Synthetic tests cover digital-silence hallucination rejection, cross-talk detection, repeated-token stitching integrity, and source/candidate safety guards. `tests/test_adversarial_cases.py` records only synthetic cases and explicitly has no clinical gold. There is no complete audio-level suite for low-volume patient denial, deceptive spoken prompts and corrupt media through the real ASR worker; resulting-note non-approval is therefore not established across the requested challenge set. - **MTA-ASR-I12:** Defined in `evaluation/asr-capability-matrix-v1.json`. It distinguishes verified local CPU profiles, conditional/unqualified CUDA profiles, and missing/corrupt weights (unavailable, no automatic download). All rows preserve the independent clinical/WER admission gate. CUDA remains a conditional statement, not a hardware validation result. - **MTA-ASR-I11:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` for the requested release check. tasks.requirement: Test phonetic confusables, sound-alike drug names, abbreviations and dose units. **
tasks.acceptance: ** Disambiguation errors and false additions reported with untouched denominators.

progress_evidence.text: - **MTA-ASR-E05:** Partial, resource-limited. The existing synthetic ASR challenge lists a generic `medical_homophone` case but contains no reviewed drug-name confusable pairs or clinical gold. The licensed development lexicon currently has one observed term, so it cannot support a meaningful sound-alike/abbreviation subgroup evaluation. Existing medication-binding checks cover explicit medication and dose swaps, but are not phonetic confusability evidence. No clinical correctness claim is made; completion requires an approved, rights-reviewed confusable set and reference labels. - **MTA-ASR-E09:** Partial, metadata-limited. Audited the six frozen development dataset manifests; none declares accent/dialect labels. No accent subgroups or accent identity were inferred from audio or names. Accordingly no accent-related accuracy result is reported. Completion requires legally available English mock data with actual reviewed metadata and a sufficient matched denominator. - **MTA-ASR-E06:** Added a finite candidate formatter limited to whitespace and case normalization for recognized numbers with supported explicit units. It verifies the before/after quantity signature, preserves the original string, never adds a missing unit, and never automatically adopts a candidate. Tests cover decimal/unit distinctions and unsupported or absent units; tests/test_asr_number_format.py: 3 passed and postprocess controls: 3 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no additional unit systems or app publication integration are claimed. - **MTA-ASR-E08:** Ran a paired local faster-whisper tiny.en development pilot on four clean paracetamol-positive turns and four nearest non-target turns. evaluation/reports/asr-lexicon-bias-pilot-v1-final.json SHA-256 d2fa02f5c7a894a8cdd57c7a6bd99136241aa1350c6b86cdd60e0150f0b616a7 binds the frozen dataset/lock, profile, lexicon and evaluator/adapter code hashes. Exact-term recall changed 1/4 to 4/4, while false insertions changed 0/4 to 1/4 and normalized WER worsened from 44/153 (28.76%) to 46/153 (30.07%); no inference failures occurred. The result is development-only, not adjudicated clinical gold. Status: partial; this small pilot shows a non-target insertion and worse overall WER, and cannot justify enabling biasing or satisfy full-cohort validation. - **MTA-ASR-E07:** Added an ASR candidate comparison wrapper around the conservative source-vs-claim rules. It flags negation-scope, medication, numeric/unit and medication-dose binding conflicts as review-required; it always keeps automatic adoption disabled and states that candidate agreement does not verify clinical truth. Mechanistic synthetic tests cover scope movement and aspirin/amlodipine dose swaps; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 5 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this comparison is rule-based, not clinically validated, and is not yet connected to every candidate workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E10:** Extended correction-suggestion records to require a source audio ID and non-empty rationale, and to retain both original and proposed text with `human_review_state=pending`, `reviewed_by=null`, and `adopted=false`. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. References are upstream TextGrid labels and optimal scoring mappings are not role confirmations. UI and backend preserve the historical source versions. Status: partial; reviewers cannot yet split, merge or reassign individual turns between anonymous speaker clusters, and a complete stale-note invalidation workflow has not been verified end to end for these edits. - **MTA-ASR-G08:** Existing failure-inclusive subgroup reports separate patient and clinician reference-role edits; the detailed development run preserves unknown roles rather than coercing them. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. progress_evidence.status_basis: Added an ASR candidate comparison wrapper around the conservative source-vs-claim rules. It flags negation-scope, medication, numeric/unit and medication-dose binding conflicts as review-required; it always keeps automatic adoption disabled and states that candidate agreement does not verify clinical truth. Mechanistic synthetic tests cover scope movement and aspirin/amlodipine dose swaps; tests/test_asr_clinical_entities.py: 5 passed. Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; this comparison is rule-based, not clinically validated, and is not yet connected to every candidate workflow. - **MTA-ASR-E10:** Extended correction-suggestion records to require a source audio ID and non-empty rationale, and to retain both original and proposed text with `human_review_state=pending`, `reviewed_by=null`, and `adopted=false`. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. Missing provenance or rationale fails closed. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 4 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the helper is not yet connected to every app candidate/version workflow, and no human-reviewed terminology correction lifecycle is active. - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. References are upstream TextGrid labels and optimal scoring mappings are not role confirmations. No VAD-turn diarization arm is included, so the requested three-way modality comparison is incomplete; clinical speaker accuracy is not claimed. - **MTA-ASR-G06:** Existing subgroup report `evaluation/reports/asr-subgroups-v1.json` (SHA-256 3d65850d0248a9ff516a51baf53ea8a3dd610b7a861e9d29a80ec0c653c67852) disaggregates overlap status, reference role and turn length; segmentation diagnostics separately mark omitted short turns and boundary clipping. tests/test_asr_subgroup_diagnostics.py and test_asr_segmentation.py: 13 passed; Ruff passes. Status: partial; upstream mock annotations are not adjudicated, and no standalone overlap detector or validated missed-short- patient-turn rate has been established. - **MTA-ASR-G07:** Existing `SpeakerRoles` UI provides audio preview and explicit role assignment; the API requires clinician confirmation and `If-Match` against the current transcript before creating a new version. UI and backend preserve the historical source versions. Status: partial; reviewers cannot yet split, merge or reassign individual turns between anonymous speaker clusters, and a complete stale-note invalidation workflow has not been verified end to end for these edits. - **MTA-ASR-G08:** Existing failure-inclusive subgroup reports separate patient and clinician reference-role edits; the detailed development run preserves unknown roles rather than coercing them. Status: partial; no patient-prioritized runtime quality control or medically critical patient omission measure is wired, and upstream role annotations are not independently adjudicated. - **MTA-ASR-G09:** Existing transcript outputs remain `review_required`, carry `speaker_unassigned`/unconfirmed role flags, and mark timing gaps as untranscribed with unknown cause. Role-dependent fact checks require confirmation or block approval rather than moving evidence across speakers. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. The full real-worker matrix across mono/stereo, silence, clipping, crosstalk and interrupted model inference has not been executed, so no real-worker speaker/timing accuracy claim is made. - **MTA-ASR-H01:** Partial. `docs/device-profile.md` defines one x86 CPU workstation with at least four threads and 16 GB RAM, without an assumed GPU. tasks.requirement: Create a candidate scoring model that combines valid acoustic evidence, decoder plausibility, consistency and risk WITHOUT using reference labels at runtime. **

progress_evidence.text: - **MTA-ASR-F05:** Partial, backend-signal blocked. Current faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters all declare n-best and confidence unsupported; none exposes a validated acoustic likelihood for candidate ranking. No numeric candidate score is synthesized. Existing source-linked checks can flag inconsistencies but cannot rank which hypothesis was spoken. Completion requires a local decoder exposing valid acoustic evidence plus development calibration data and a frozen policy. - **MTA-ASR-F07:** Added an early-exit eligibility rule that requires every reason-coded diagnostic to be explicitly present with provenance and clear; missing diagnostics or any observed risk routes to re-decode/review. Measured silence with empty text is separately identified. tests/test_asr_risk_selector.py: 10 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no upstream signals are wired into this rule, it does not yet save runtime compute, and recall of actual errors has not been measured. - **MTA-ASR-F08:** Partial, annotation-limited. No clinician-adjudicated span-level critical-error labels or validated risk-selector outputs are available, so critical miss rate, safe-case false alarms, selected-audio coverage, and equal-compute random/control curves cannot be estimated honestly. Developer-authored synthetic fixtures remain mechanism tests and are not presented as coverage results. Completion requires reviewed development labels and matched selector/control inference receipts. - **MTA-ASR-F09:** Partial, model-signal blocked. Faster-whisper, Omi and Parakeet adapters explicitly return confidence unsupported and uncalibrated; the deterministic risk score remains null. No reliability diagram or ECE is computed from heuristics or invented posteriors. Calibration work requires a backend with genuine score signals and a separate labeled development set. - **MTA-ASR-F06:** Partial. Existing repair jobs cap each requested crop at 120 seconds, validate source authorization/version/hash, admit model memory before inference, and retry worker jobs at most three times. Candidate output remains separate from the source transcript. No hard wall-clock cancellation is enforced inside a native model call; a lease heartbeat is not an inference timeout. A process-isolated inference deadline and end-to-end compute budget remain outstanding. - **MTA-ASR-F04:** Extended advisory candidate checks so changes to negation and allergy polarity are explicitly flagged alongside drug and dose/unit changes. Raw wording remains immutable, all proposals remain pending review, and nothing is auto-adopted. tests/test_asr_postprocess.py: 5 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; the rule helper is not integrated into every text-generation/publication path and its heuristics are not clinically validated. - **MTA-ASR-F10:** Added a deterministic immutable candidate-receipt builder binding audio and transcript IDs/digests, source span, original hypothesis, alternatives, decoder/profile digests, selection policy version, and abstention. Receipts preserve review-required/non-adopted status, reject reference-text fields, verify their semantic digest, and write exclusively. tests/test_asr_candidate_receipt.py: 3 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; current application retranscription does not yet persist this unified receipt, and deterministic inference replay is unverified. - **MTA-ASR-G01:** Transcript segments now persist `timestamp_kind` separately from model-estimated segment bounds. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Existing timestamp checks reject malformed/out-of-bounds segment times and explicitly leave `word_alignment_validated=false`; they do not claim alignment proves a word was spoken. No acoustic support test for inserted words can be run until a qualified local aligner and independent audio-supported fixtures exist. - **MTA-ASR-G03:** Existing audio provenance maps source PCM crops and channel selections to parent sample offsets, and resampled mappings fail closed unless source origin and group delay are measured. `tests/test_audio_provenance.py` covers crop mapping, measured resampling, monotonic offsets and unknown-delay rejection. Status: partial; mapping checks do not cover a forced-alignment runtime, which is unavailable under G02, or a full end-to-end alignment round trip. - **MTA-ASR-G04:** Existing diarization output keeps `speaker_id` values separate from role labels; roles start `unknown`/`unconfirmed`, with clinician confirmation required. Channel-derived IDs are explicitly marked as not verified speakers, and observed-channel mapping never infers roles. `tests/test_diarization_policy.py` and `test_asr_evaluation_contract.py`: 13 passed; Ruff passes. `test_channels.py` separately asserts unconfirmed roles. Status: partial; no identity/role accuracy or clinician confirmation has been established for these R&D runs. - **MTA-ASR-G05:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/speaker-comparison-2026-10-26.json` contains matched fixed-window and separate-channel conditions for three consultations, with DER and role error timing. Status: partial; upstream mock annotations are not adjudicated, and no standalone overlap detector or validated missed-short- patient-turn rate has been established. - **MTA-ASR-G07:** Existing `SpeakerRoles` UI provides audio preview and explicit role assignment; the API requires clinician confirmation and `If-Match` against the current transcript before creating a new version. UI and backend preserve the historical source versions. Status: partial; reviewers cannot yet split, merge or reassign individual turns between anonymous speaker clusters, and a complete stale-note invalidation workflow has not been verified end to end for these edits. - **MTA-ASR-G08:** Existing failure-inclusive subgroup reports separate patient and clinician reference-role edits; the detailed development run preserves unknown roles rather than coercing them. Status: partial; no patient-prioritized runtime quality control or medically critical patient omission measure is wired, and upstream role annotations are not independently adjudicated. - **MTA-ASR-G09:** Existing transcript outputs remain `review_required`, carry `speaker_unassigned`/unconfirmed role flags, and mark timing gaps as untranscribed with unknown cause. Role-dependent fact checks require confirmation or block approval rather than moving evidence across speakers. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. The full real-worker matrix across mono/stereo, silence, clipping, crosstalk and interrupted model inference has not been executed, so no real-worker speaker/timing accuracy claim is made. - **MTA-ASR-H01:** Partial. `docs/device-profile.md` defines one x86 CPU workstation with at least four threads and 16 GB RAM, without an assumed GPU. The frozen detailed set contains eight unique consultation groups across 16 paired clean/noisy recordings (1.32 recorded hours, with shared source content across conditions); labels are upstream mock references and are not independently adjudicated. This supports offline inference experiments, not training a speech foundation model from scratch. Current benchmark source manifests and local model profiles bind dataset/model revisions and license identifiers; lexicon construction further requires rights-reviewed development manifests and verified locks. No gated or restricted model/data was used in the reported local runs, and no derived training artifact exists. This is a preflight for the evaluated assets, not authorization to train on any additional source; each future training input and derived artifact needs its own rights review. - **MTA-ASR-H03:** Partial. Development manifests identify consultation-group IDs, and `evaluation/acceptance-reservation-v1.json` reserves three groups before inference for future independent annotation. Current evaluation uses development groups only; there is no training split or training manifest because no adaptation has been run. Group separation does not prove speaker, site, device or model-training independence, and no shared-speaker leakage check is possible from the available metadata. - **MTA-ASR-H04:** Not run. No training augmentation artifacts were generated. Existing gain/filter/noise-suppression work is paired inference-time signal processing with source provenance; it is not relabeled training data or a training augmentation gain. Any future licensed development augmentation needs reproducible seeds, parent/derived hashes and label-preservation checks. - **MTA-ASR-H05:** Not run. Existing ROVER and hotword experiments are inference-time candidate generation/decoding comparisons, not trained correction or reranking components. No cross-fitted training table was created; reserved acceptance groups remain excluded. A future confusion table would need group-level train/development boundaries and source-linked labels before any component is fit. - **MTA-ASR-H06:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. Existing inference profiles provide converted/quantized decoder artifacts, not an approved training architecture, optimizer recipe or adapter checkpoint. The reference host has CPU-only capacity and no qualified training accelerator; no LoRA/rescoring training has been simulated or claimed. - **MTA-ASR-H07:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No candidate has genuine calibrated acoustic scores or a disjoint group-level calibration corpus; current backend confidence is explicitly unsupported. F09 records the same evidence gap. No reliability curves or selection thresholds are fabricated. - **MTA-ASR-H08:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No independently verified clinician-confirmed correction set is available. Existing UI edits are source-versioned operational corrections, not research training labels; synthetic fixtures and developer-authored proposals are never treated as clinician signatures or automatic self-training input. - **MTA-ASR-H09:** Not implemented. There is no training/adapter corpus or clinician-correction lexicon state to remove, and no future-training lineage deletion mechanism has been tested. Current E01 lexicon entries bind to licensed development-manifest digests and are write-once artifacts; that provenance is not equivalent to revocation/unlearning propagation. - **MTA-ASR-H10:** No adaptation-attributable gain is established (`null`). The primary WER endpoint is frozen, but the safety-gate preregistration is incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I02:** Partial. Faster-whisper output is labeled `native_segment`; other engines default to `unknown`, and transcript-level word alignment is explicitly `not_provided`. tests/test_transcript_timestamp_integrity.py and test_timestamp_registry.py: 7 passed; Ruff and format checks pass. Status: partial; no native word timestamps or validated forced aligner are available, and segment bounds do not establish word alignment. - **MTA-ASR-G02:** Partial, local-aligner blocked. Repository dependency and model inventories contain no validated English forced aligner. Status: partial; no patient-prioritized runtime quality control or medically critical patient omission measure is wired, and upstream role annotations are not independently adjudicated. - **MTA-ASR-G09:** Existing transcript outputs remain `review_required`, carry `speaker_unassigned`/unconfirmed role flags, and mark timing gaps as untranscribed with unknown cause. Role-dependent fact checks require confirmation or block approval rather than moving evidence across speakers. Status: partial; policy behavior is covered by transcript/review tests, but there is no comprehensive UI test proving every clinically role-dependent workflow blocks on unknown timing and role metadata. - **MTA-ASR-G10:** Partial. The frozen detailed set contains eight unique consultation groups across 16 paired clean/noisy recordings (1.32 recorded hours, with shared source content across conditions); labels are upstream mock references and are not independently adjudicated. Current benchmark source manifests and local model profiles bind dataset/model revisions and license identifiers; lexicon construction further requires rights-reviewed development manifests and verified locks. No gated or restricted model/data was used in the reported local runs, and no derived training artifact exists. This is a preflight for the evaluated assets, not authorization to train on any additional source; each future training input and derived artifact needs its own rights review. - **MTA-ASR-H03:** Partial. Development manifests identify consultation-group IDs, and `evaluation/acceptance-reservation-v1.json` reserves three groups before inference for future independent annotation. Current evaluation uses development groups only; there is no training split or training manifest because no adaptation has been run. Group separation does not prove speaker, site, device or model-training independence, and no shared-speaker leakage check is possible from the available metadata. - **MTA-ASR-H04:** Not run. No training augmentation artifacts were generated. Existing gain/filter/noise-suppression work is paired inference-time signal processing with source provenance; it is not relabeled training data or a training augmentation gain. Any future licensed development augmentation needs reproducible seeds, parent/derived hashes and label-preservation checks. - **MTA-ASR-H05:** Not run. Existing ROVER and hotword experiments are inference-time candidate generation/decoding comparisons, not trained correction or reranking components. No cross-fitted training table was created; reserved acceptance groups remain excluded. A future confusion table would need group-level train/development boundaries and source-linked labels before any component is fit. - **MTA-ASR-H06:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. Existing inference profiles provide converted/quantized decoder artifacts, not an approved training architecture, optimizer recipe or adapter checkpoint. The reference host has CPU-only capacity and no qualified training accelerator; no LoRA/rescoring training has been simulated or claimed. - **MTA-ASR-H07:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE`. No candidate has genuine calibrated acoustic scores or a disjoint group-level calibration corpus; current backend confidence is explicitly unsupported. F09 records the same evidence gap. No correction model, LoRA adapter or rescoring model was trained. The E08 hotword pilot changes decoding only and worsened aggregate WER on its small matched subset; it cannot be credited as an adaptation gain. - **MTA-ASR-I01:** Partial. `evaluation/selection-policy.json` and frozen evaluation contracts predeclare failure-inclusive normalized WER and retain the unchanged <=5% ceiling; existing reports cannot weaken it. Clinical critical-error and patient-role non-inferiority tolerances are still pending a clinical owner, and no independent adjudicated acceptance set is available. The primary WER endpoint is frozen, but the safety-gate preregistration is incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I02:** Partial. Existing frozen reports provide identical-input comparisons for fixed/overlap/speech-aware/context segmentation and for matched decoder/consensus arms; the E08 term-bias pilot also pairs baseline and biased decoding on identical crops. The full declared matrix (VAD-only, terminology-only, repair-only and full pipeline under equal compute) has not been run on one frozen cohort, so no end-to-end method attribution is claimed. - **MTA-ASR-I03:** `FAIL` for every currently evaluated model/system profile. The unchanged admission ceiling is normalized WER <=5%; the best expanded short-clip model result is still 8.70%, and full-consultation/detailed runs are worse. The E08 pilot's false insertion is a development signal, not a clinical error rate. Abstentions remain review-required and cannot be counted as successful corrections. - **MTA-ASR-I05:** Engineering system path is now exercised by `tests/test_real_local_asr_workflow.py`: the existing licensed PriMock57 patient utterance passes through upload, PCM ingest, the actual locally installed tiny.en Faster Whisper model, immutable native-timestamped transcript, versioned source review, note verification, approval and integrity-checked JSON export. The test passed against the current local model artifacts. Review and approval actions are scripted for this public mock fixture; they do not represent clinician review, clinical validity or user acceptance. The frozen WER and independent safety gates remain separate. - **MTA-ASR-I06:** Partial. High-risk medication, dose/unit, negation and allergy edits are emitted as pending, non-adopted suggestions while original ASR text remains intact (`tests/test_asr_postprocess.py`: 5 passed). Transcript edits create immutable child versions and stale approvals fail closed; span retranscription checks bind to the current source/audio. This is software guard coverage only: the broader review/retranscription workflow test command did not finish in this run, and coverage does not establish clinician review quality. No automatic adoption path was found in these reviewed correction modules. - **MTA-ASR-I07:** Partial. `evaluation/reports/paired-asr-bootstrap-v1.json` reports paired clean-versus-distracted WER deltas using consultation-level resampling (10,000 deterministic iterations, 95% percentile intervals) and records both arms and failed statuses for each pair. The report does not stratify paired uncertainty by clinical term or speaker, and preserved failure statuses are not adjudicated clinical error estimates; the requested full uncertainty analysis remains incomplete. - **MTA-ASR-I08:** Partial. Existing compute Pareto receipts report measured case wall time and RTF percentiles for selected inference profiles; worker receipts also retain per-job wall time. Model cards and a negative-experiment index exist, and benchmark receipts bind runs to dataset/model/source digests. However, the index is a bounded historical inventory and the reporting artifacts do not currently provide one reproducible publication package with every requested ablation/error table regenerated from source-bound receipts. Clinical-gold and admission claims remain explicitly absent. - **MTA-ASR-I10:** Partial. Synthetic tests cover digital-silence hallucination rejection, cross-talk detection, repeated-token stitching integrity, and source/candidate safety guards. `tests/test_adversarial_cases.py` records only synthetic cases and explicitly has no clinical gold. There is no complete audio-level suite for low-volume patient denial, deceptive spoken prompts and corrupt media through the real ASR worker; resulting-note non-approval is therefore not established across the requested challenge set. - **MTA-ASR-I12:** Defined in `evaluation/asr-capability-matrix-v1.json`. It distinguishes verified local CPU profiles, conditional/unqualified CUDA profiles, and missing/corrupt weights (unavailable, no automatic download). All rows preserve the independent clinical/WER admission gate. CUDA remains a conditional statement, not a hardware validation result. - **MTA-ASR-I11:** `BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` for the requested release check. The repository CI workflow declares Python quality/full-suite, frontend, PostgreSQL and container jobs, but GitHub returned no status checks for the current source commit `8d93b88f4a170d12e2e64a7b28a3ae23e1fb9060`. The latest available local acceptance receipt is from an earlier source commit and records a timed-out full backend run plus missing PyAV, PostgreSQL DSN and Docker. Those results are not promoted as exact-HEAD evidence; all required exact-HEAD CI lanes remain unverified. - **MTA-ASR-I13:** Partial. The clinician source-review screen supports keyboard-operated source-interval playback, transcript text edits, and saving corrections as a new version. The read-only ASR error-review packet shows waveform clips/audio, source intervals and candidate alternatives, but is a research/development tool, not the clinician queue. The clinician screen does not present reason-coded ASR alternatives as an uncertain-span queue, and no scripted usability acceptance was run for that workflow. - **MTA-ASR-I14:** Published `evaluation/reports/asr-objective-release-v1.json` with objective-level `FAIL`/`BLOCKED_MISSING_RESOURCE` decisions for model qualification, clinical safety, end-to-end product acceptance and engineering CI. TypeScript and the production build pass. The frozen WER and independent safety gates remain separate. - **MTA-ASR-I06:** Partial. High-risk medication, dose/unit, negation and allergy edits are emitted as pending, non-adopted suggestions while original ASR text remains intact (`tests/test_asr_postprocess.py`: 5 passed).
